newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--The danger of the crisis at the Athens Stock Exchange expanding hangs over the bourse as brokers and government attempt to find a compromise that will see a resumption of trading.

--Today's informal inner cabinet meeting is considered to be crucial for the taking of final decisions on the government's economic policy and the 1997 budget. The government is concerned about adverse reactions from ruling party PASOK MPs, particularly in light of the proposed abolition of tax breaks for MPs.
--New state titles will be issued by December to cover state lending needs amounting to one trillion drachmas.
--Civil servants demand higher wage increases than those foreseen in the government's proposed wage scale.

--Former conservative prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis will absent himself from today's main opposition New Democracy party Political Council, called to discuss possible disciplinary procedures for those disputing a recent truce over the ND leadership issue.

--Questions have been aired over the last days of the late founder and leader of ruling party PASOK Andreas Papandreou. Former health minister and Papandreou's doctor Dimitris Kremastinos claims that Papandreou was receiving alternative medicine without his knowledge. A prosecutor is examining the possibility of a preliminary inquiry.
--Alarm bells go off at the Athens Stock Exchange. The government tells brokers to clear up the situation or they will not be allowed back into the bourse.
--Teachers hit the streets today to demand more positions in state schools, education funding and pay increases.
--Another eight brokerage firms are implicated in the scandal at the Athens Stock Exchange while prosecution of violators has not yet been ruled out.

--A new opinion poll shows the majority in favour of the tax on real estate but against increasing wealth indicators. An overwhelming majority support the government's move to abolish tax breaks for MPs, journalists, judges and other professional groups.
--The number of drug users in Greece doubles: 600 dead so far this year from drug use.
--Insurance firms propose a 25-40 percent increase in premiums on car insurance as of December.

--The developments at the bourse have placed 145 mutual funds and the titles market in danger. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou urges the bourse to resume trading as soon as possible. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
